Cover mechanic. Every shooter (of any genre) you play requires at least SOME cover to dodge incoming fire. But games like COD just have you crouch behind something while say, Killzone allows you to pop over cover and fire back without exposing yourself completely.

OK, not a movie, but "This is Jinsy" on Hulu. I laughed so hard and still thought, "wtf did I just watch".

For me, the strangest movie I've seen recently was Chocolate.

At first I thought it was going to be a revenge film where two lovers reunite after being forced apart by rival gangs.

Nope, it's about an autistic girl who learns martial arts from watching television and her fat friend who encourages her to beat up guys for money. It gets stranger too.

SPOILER!!!

Near the end of the film, the girl's friend is kidnapped and so is her mother. She goes and confronts the boss and she starts fighting all his thugs. Then, HE comes in. Another autistic person. The guy is wearing a track suit similar to one would expect a squatting russian to wear. And I swear, this guy must be the most twitchiest bastard I've seen, because that's all he does. Apparently, even the boss knows the value of autists, because he employed the only other martial art autist in the city.

I realized then, I was watching a strange movie when I saw two autistic people fighting each other to the death.

Anyways, she wins by out autism-ing the twitchy tracksuit boy by copying his moves, which I might add, were twitchy semi-break dance moves.

EDIT: Apparently, tracksuit boy isn't autistic, he has tourrets. So it wasn't two autistic people fighting to the death. No, it was two people killing each other with their disabilities.

I saw Heavy Metal on an Encore/Starz free weekend when I was really too young and didn't realize there was a difference between cartoons and adult animation. Being John Malkovich is another -- I saw that on an HBO free weekend (funny how the only time I see anything worth watching is when the premium channels offer it as a trial) and was interested to watch it because I really like John Cusack. Boy is that movie bizarre. I figured out later that it really should have been called Being Charlie Kaufman because while Malkovich is an odd dude himself, Charlie Kaufman the screenwriter is whose kooky brain that story really came out of.

I also saw Felix the Cat on the Disney channel, which is still a pretty bizarre movie despite it being ostensibly for kids. I mean what's up with the body-less winged creatures who try to decapitate their prey, and the Master Cylinder thing? I now realize that 1980-89 was a massive acid trip for the world of cinema.
